mood.summary: Fear is still running high. On Nov 5 the S&P 500 fell 4.4% and the Nasdaq slid into a correction, the worst day since April 2025, on worries that election results will slow AI and data-centre spending. The Fear & Greed index sits in Extreme Fear at 20, and bearish individual investors outnumber bulls by about 14 points. Stocks are bouncing on Nov 6 after a strong jobs report (165,000 jobs vs about 60,000 expected), but that also firmed bets on a December Fed rate hike.

items.name: SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust
items.about: Tracks the S&P 500 index of large US companies.
items.why: The S&P 500 ETF fell 4.4% on a broad, tech-led sell-off, its low coming near the close. News headlines tie the drop to worries about AI data-center spending and regulation after the midterm elections, plus a weak Qualcomm outlook; posts say hedge funds were hit hard.

items.name: Invesco QQQ Trust Series 1
items.about: Tracks the Nasdaq-100 index of the largest Nasdaq-listed non-financial companies.
items.why: The fund fell 6.4%, one of its steepest days in years, as chip and AI-linked names led the market lower. Reports said the Nasdaq Composite closed in correction territory, more than 10% below its record set last month.

items.name: NVIDIA Corp
items.about: Designs GPUs and systems used for AI computing and graphics.
items.why: Shares fell 9.2% as semiconductor stocks sold off on concerns about AI data-center spending and possible regulation after the midterms. News reports put the loss in tech market value near US$1.7 trillion for the day; posts say traders are buying puts and some dip-buying calls.

items.name: Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3X Shares
items.about: Leveraged fund seeking three times the daily return of a semiconductor index.
items.why: The 3x fund fell 38.6% because the chip index it tracks fell roughly 12% in a day, with the leverage tripling the move. Volume was near 490 million shares; posts say some holders lost large parts of their accounts while others are buying the dip.

items.name: Applied Optoelectronics Inc
items.about: Makes optical transceivers and laser components used in data centers and cable networks.
items.why: Shares dropped 21.1% with the AI-hardware group; posts say earnings are due soon and that the stock is down about 60% in a month. No company-specific announcement was found, so the sector sell-off appears to be the main driver.

items.name: IREN Limited
items.about: Operates data centers for AI cloud computing and bitcoin mining.
items.why: Shares fell 15.8% despite a results release; posts say fiscal Q1 revenue was about US$228M versus roughly US$221M expected, down 5% from a year ago, with AI cloud around US$200M of it. The drop coincided with the broader AI-infrastructure sell-off.

items.name: Micron Technology Inc
items.about: Makes DRAM and NAND memory chips, including high-bandwidth memory for AI servers.
items.why: Shares fell 17.5% in the chip sell-off, with one report citing fears that slower AI data-center expansion would dent memory demand. Posts say memory peers also fell even after strong earnings, raised guidance and buybacks.

items.name: Wendy's Co
items.about: Operates and franchises the Wendy's fast-food restaurant chain.
items.why: Shares rose 3.6% to US$7.93 while the market fell sharply. No new announcement was found; posts say attention is on investor Nelson Peltz's stake, and a news report from February said his firm had called the stock undervalued and was exploring strategic options.

items.name: Vanguard S&P 500 ETF
items.about: Tracks the S&P 500 index at a low fee.
items.why: The fund fell 4.4% along with the S&P 500 in a tech-led sell-off. Posts say the index touched its 200-day average and are split between buying the dip and expecting more selling.

items.name: ProShares UltraPro QQQ
items.about: Leveraged fund seeking three times the daily return of the Nasdaq-100.
items.why: The 3x fund fell 19.0% after the Nasdaq-100 dropped about 6.4%, and posts say it is down roughly 40% in a week. Volume was above 214 million shares as traders bought and sold the swing.

items.name: Advanced Micro Devices Inc
items.about: Designs CPUs, GPUs and AI accelerators.
items.why: Shares fell 17.2% on heavy chatter, with posts referring to its recent earnings report and the wider AI-chip sell-off. News reports named AMD among the biggest decliners, down about 15-16% at points in the day.

items.name: SPDR Gold Shares ETF
items.about: Holds physical gold bullion and tracks its price.
items.why: The fund rose 0.8% as stocks fell; a headline said gold rallied above US$4,100 as falling Treasury yields and fading rate-hike bets supported it. Posts note it closed below its open, so the safe-haven move was modest.

items.name: Cloudflare Inc
items.about: Provides network security, content delivery and edge computing services.
items.why: Shares fell 8.5% to the close and slid further after hours as the stock heads into earnings, listed after the close on Nov 5. Posts say the AI sell-off and a heavy put share of options flow are weighing.

items.name: Figma
items.about: Makes the Figma collaborative interface-design and prototyping software.
items.why: Shares fell 17.0% a day after its scheduled Q3 report (Nov 4, after close); the results coverage could not be found. Posts say investors are worried about AI competition and point to a valuation of under 5x forward sales with about US$1.7B in net cash.

items.name: Celsius Holdings Inc
items.about: Sells Celsius-branded fitness and energy drinks.
items.why: Shares ended down 2.3% after spiking above US$33 early, a milder move than the market. Posts say quarterly revenue grew about 36% with sharply higher earnings, and that Monster Beverage reports after the close.

items.name: Redwire Corp
items.about: Builds space infrastructure including solar arrays, sensors and in-space manufacturing.
items.why: Shares fell 20.0%, the largest drop among space names according to posts, which say it is down about 45% in a month. No company-specific news was found; the move looks tied to the high-beta sell-off.

items.name: Biocryst Pharmaceuticals Inc.
items.about: Develops rare-disease drugs, including the hereditary angioedema treatment Orladeyo.
items.why: Shares fell 7.7% on a sharply down day for small caps. No catalyst was found; posts say the stock has traded between US$7 and US$9 for much of three years and see it near support.

items.name: Xeris Biopharma Holdings Inc
items.about: Sells specialty drugs including Gvoke glucagon and Recorlev, and develops pipeline therapies.
items.why: Shares jumped 25.6% on about 10 million shares, a rare green day. No confirming news was found; posts say about 8 million shares are sold short and discuss long-term revenue targets and takeover potential.

items.name: VanEck Semiconductor ETF
items.about: Holds a basket of large semiconductor companies.
items.why: The fund fell 11.5% as Nvidia, Micron and AMD led the sell-off; reports described chip ETFs' worst day since March 2020. Options flow was heavy on both sides, according to posts.

items.name: Dutch Bros Inc
items.about: Operates a drive-thru coffee and beverage chain.
items.why: Shares fell 21.3% after the Q3 report on Nov 4. The company's filing shows revenue up 29.8% to US$549.8M, same-shop sales up 4.4% and 48 new shops, plus a goal of 250 openings in 2027; posts say the market sell-off added pressure.
